pr_title: Wire up `internal-inline-outputs` requirement with RE API
pr_body:
In-memory outputs marked with the `internal-inline-outputs` execution requirement are now added to the `inline_output_files` hint field of the remote execution and remote cache API, potentially saving a round trip on files that are unconditionally read by Bazel client after spawn execution.

Support for output file inlining has been added to the remote worker implementation.

Fixes #8421

issue_context.title: implement action output inlining for remote execution
comments: Marking untriaged so that the team can decide if this is still needed.
It doesn't seem high priority at this time as there are a number of other possible performance improvements that'll have a bigger impact.

Hi there! We're doing a clean up of old issues and will be closing this one. Please reopen if you’d like to discuss anything further. We’ll respond as soon as we have the bandwidth/resources to do so.

From offline discussion: https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/pull/23428 will mark in-memory outputs (currently: `.d`, `.jdeps` and `unused_inputs_list` files) as inlinable. Beyond that, we should consider marking any output that will be immediately downloaded (per the `--remote_download_outputs` and `--remote_download_regex` flags) as inlinable. I'm not convinced that we need to provide a general facility for rule authors to mark outputs as inlinable, since covering these two cases should provide most of the performance benefit.

@tjgq Is it clear that inlining arbitrary outputs that are downloaded with BwoB is a win? For `.d` and `.jdeps` files this is definitely true since they are read synchronously in and thus block the action that ran the spawn. But wouldn't `--remote_download_regex` downloads happen off the critical path? Inlining is also constrained to 4 MiB files.

That's a good point - forcing the download to occur synchronously might very well undo the gains of avoiding the extra round trip. I suppose we could try it out and see what happens, but it's definitely not a clear win.

(Also note: while we *could* download outputs in the background, they currently block completion of the spawn that produces them: https://cs.opensource.google/bazel/bazel/+/master:src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/remote/RemoteExecutionService.java;l=1239;drc=d91e05e4a82e61720d41e64b81d4b36924b1c398).
I wasn't aware of that. It may very well be better to lift that restriction first before we extend the scope of inlining.
Yeah, I'm now of the opinion that we should move downloads to the background (other than the in-memory case) and not bother with inlining them at all.

A fix for this issue has been included in [Bazel 7.4.0 RC1](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/releases/tag/7.4.0rc1). Please test out the release candidate and report any issues as soon as possible.
If you're using Bazelisk, you can point to the latest RC by setting `USE_BAZEL_VERSION=7.4.0rc1`. Thanks!
